clue.text: Stop, for example, horse eating root containing sulphur

indicators.note: the horse swallows what follows, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: a roan is a horse with a coat flecked with white

indicators.note: the root word holds the element symbol within it

parts.note: to dig is to root about in the soil
S is the chemical symbol for sulphur

explanation.surface: A horse chews a root that happens to contain sulphur.
explanation.definitionFit: A Stop sign is one example of a traffic signpost at the roadside.

clue.text: Pot — container upturned

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned upside down means the word is read from the bottom up

parts.note: a drawer is a sliding container in furniture

explanation.surface: A pot is a container that has been tipped over.
explanation.definitionFit: A pot is a prize or jackpot, money won as a prize.

clue.text: A carnival vehicle appearing amphibious?

parts.note: a float is a decorated vehicle in a parade or carnival

explanation.surface: A parade float looks as if it could take to the water.
explanation.definitionFit: Something amphibious can stay on water, floating; the question mark admits the stretch.

clue.text: Reform this law or its public demonstration?

indicators.note: to reform is to form again, so the letters of these words are rebuilt

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a law should be reformed or put on public display.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of THIS LAW OR, prompted by 'Reform', sits beside a definition that refers back to the law in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A staged trial held to make a political example is a public demonstration of the law's power.

clue.text: Air evidence hanky wasn't used?

definitions.meaning: an air is a tune, here a famous old English song
someone who wipes a runny nose on the cuffs instead of a handkerchief leaves telltale coloured cuffs

explanation.definitionFit: The Tudor tune of that title is a well-known English air, often credited to Henry VIII.

clue.text: Swimmer has to dry back

indicators.note: back says the whole string is read in reverse

parts.note: brut describes very dry champagne or wine

explanation.surface: A swimmer has to dry off its back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the joined pieces round as one run; brut is the label on the driest champagne.
explanation.definitionFit: A turbot is a large flatfish, so a swimmer in the sea.

clue.text: Doubly empty state having injected heroin? Yes!

indicators.note: something injected goes inside, so the drug sits in the middle of the pair
doubly means the emptied state is written twice over
empty means the inside of the word is removed, leaving only its outer letters

parts.note: Utah is a US state
H is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: An addict, doubly empty after injecting heroin, cries yes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' leaves UH from UTAH; 'Doubly' gives UHUH; 'having injected' puts H between the two.
explanation.definitionFit: This informal grunt is a spoken way of agreeing, an affirmative like yes.

clue.text: One stops leaks on top of a blue house

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece is placed above the next

parts.note: a bung is a stopper that plugs a hole
blue can mean sad, low in spirits

explanation.surface: Something to stop leaks is put on top of a blue house.
explanation.definitionFit: A bungalow is a one-storey house.

clue.text: Elmer Fudd's dealing with the singing of Sylvester's foe?

indicators.note: the cartoon hunter Elmer Fudd says W for R, so the word comes out of his mouth changed in sound

parts.note: treating means dealing with or handling

explanation.surface: A cartoon character mangles a word while describing the song of a cartoon bird.
explanation.walkthrough: Sylvester is the cartoon cat whose foe is the canary Tweety; Elmer Fudd turns every R into W when he speaks, so his 'treating' is heard as birdsong.
explanation.definitionFit: Birdsong is called tweeting, so the canary's singing is fittingly named in this pun.

clue.text: King held in admiration during conflict finds easy victory

indicators.note: during places that inside the conflict word

parts.note: war is armed conflict

indicators.note: held in puts the king inside the admiration word

parts.note: love is warm admiration
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A king admired in wartime wins an easy victory.
explanation.definitionFit: A walkover is a win gained without real opposition, an easy victory.

clue.text: Chinaman given English coins

parts.note: Chang is a common Chinese surname, standing for a Chinese man

explanation.surface: A Chinese man is handed some English coins.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose coins are called change, small money in the pocket.

clue.text: Is a punch in the stomach so awesome?

definitions.text: Is a punch in the stomach
definitions.meaning: a blow to the stomach knocks the wind out of you, literally robbing you of air

explanation.definitionFit: A breathtaking view is astonishing, one so awesome it stops you breathing for a moment.

clue.text: Food right for the oven

parts.note: an oast is a kiln or oven for drying hops

explanation.surface: This food is just right for putting in the oven.
explanation.definitionFit: A roast is a joint of meat cooked as a meal, a kind of food.

clue.text: Direction taken by spaceman or the astronomer

indicators.note: the letters are carried by, held within, the following words

explanation.surface: A spaceman or an astronomer chooses which way to head.
explanation.definitionFit: This compass point lying between two cardinal points is a direction.

clue.text: Manufacture smooth gift for the soppy lot

parts.note: to mill is to process or manufacture in a mill
to sand is to smooth with sandpaper
a boon is a gift or blessing

explanation.surface: A factory produces a smooth gift for the sentimental.
explanation.walkthrough: MILLS AND BOON is a British publisher of romantic fiction.
explanation.definitionFit: The firm's slushy romance novels make the publisher's name shorthand for soppy, sentimental writing.

clue.text: Carol's sleep male disturbed during shift

indicators.note: during puts the rearranged letters inside the garment

parts.note: a shift is a simple straight dress

indicators.note: disturbed letters are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: Carollers' sleep, a man is disturbed during a work shift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carol' is not a woman: the carol is O Little Town of Bethlehem, with its line 'Above thy deep and dreamless sleep'.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes sleep in the carol's line, so it stands for the kind of sleep the carol sings of.

clue.text: Our neighbour has to maintain a certain force to produce methane

parts.note: Mars is a planet neighbouring Earth

indicators.note: to maintain is to hold, so one word keeps the other inside it

parts.note: taken as written
g is the symbol for the force of gravity

explanation.surface: A neighbouring planet keeps up some force to give off methane.
explanation.definitionFit: Marsh gas is the common name for methane released by rotting matter in wetlands.

clue.text: Bird, common type pinching monarch's bottom

indicators.note: pinching means grabbing and holding inside

parts.note: a peasant is a common, lowly person

indicators.note: in a down clue the bottom letter of a word is its last

explanation.surface: A commoner pinches the king's bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: A pheasant is a long-tailed game bird.

clue.text: A cold fish claiming she's failing

parts.note: a chill is a cold

indicators.note: claiming means taking hold of, so the fish wraps round the pronoun

parts.note: an eel is a fish
the possessive gives the pronoun she

explanation.surface: A cold fish insists that she is failing.
explanation.definitionFit: An Achilles heel is a weak point, a personal failing.

clue.text: Toss last of butter in with last of margarine

indicators.note: in puts that letter inside the given word
last of picks the final letter of butter
last of again picks the final letter of margarine

explanation.surface: A cook adds the last of the butter with the last of the margarine.
explanation.definitionFit: To writhe is to toss and turn in pain or discomfort.

clue.text: Where hymn performed by word of mouth, sung

parts.note: CH is the abbreviation for church, where hymns are sung
oral means spoken, by word of mouth

explanation.surface: A hymn performed where it is passed on by mouth is sung.
explanation.definitionFit: Choral music is written to be sung by a choir.

clue.text: Neighbours, perhaps, like this: a poet and artist

parts.note: so means in this way, like this
Alexander Pope was an English poet
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: The neighbours enjoy a poet and an artist living in this way.
explanation.walkthrough: Neighbours is an Australian TV soap long popular in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: The long-running Australian drama is one example of a television soap.

clue.text: One may be stuffed, none survive

parts.note: O, the figure zero, means none
to live is to survive

explanation.surface: Someone is stuffed and none survive.
explanation.definitionFit: An olive is often stuffed with pimento or cheese.

clue.text: Storm before the showers?

definitions.meaning: to storm is to stride angrily
proverbially April brings showers, so the month before them

explanation.definitionFit: To march off is to storm off; and the month preceding April's showers is the third.

clue.text: Expecting to find a 5 in part of crossword

indicators.note: in places the inner pieces inside the grid

parts.note: the grid is part of a crossword
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: A solver expects to find a reference to 5 somewhere in the crossword grid.
explanation.walkthrough: '5' looks like a cross-reference to 5-across, but it is just the number, written in Roman numerals.
explanation.definitionFit: Gravid is a formal word for pregnant, that is expecting a baby.

clue.text: Quality of goddess in wood

indicators.note: in puts the goddess inside the wood

parts.note: fir is a softwood timber
Vesta is the Roman goddess of the hearth

explanation.surface: A goddess with real quality is carved in wood.
explanation.definitionFit: A five-star rating marks top quality, as in luxury hotels.

clue.text: Model, a dolly

definitions.meaning: a model sits for a painter, a person who poses
in cricket a dolly is an easy catch, also called a gift

explanation.walkthrough: A dolly in British cricket slang is an easy catch, as simple as a sitting target.
explanation.definitionFit: A painter's model is a sitter, and an easy chance in sport is a sitter too.

clue.text: Spurs' misery at the finish

parts.note: to egg someone on is to spur them on
hell is utter misery

explanation.surface: Tottenham Hotspur fans suffer misery at the end of the game.
explanation.walkthrough: Spurs is the nickname of Tottenham Hotspur, a London football club; here it is a verb meaning urges.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggshell is a paint finish with a slight sheen.
